newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW - Mercury says PNZ j/v makes float certain.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mercury says PNZ j/v makes float certain.

text.p: Mercury Energy Ltd chief executive Wayne Gilbert said on Tuesday the settling of a takeover battle for fellow Auckland power distributor, Power New Zealand Ltd, made flotation of Mercury a certainty.
"The float now is certain and it will be sooner rather than later," he told Reuters in a phone interview.
Gilbert said the preparation of a prospectus would mean the float would come next year rather than this year. The company's board is meeting this week to consider the issue, he said.
Mercury had previously planned to float but its opposed takeover bid for Power NZ caused it to delay the float.
Earlier, Mercury announced it had joined with rival bidder Utilicorp NZ, a unit of Utilicorp United Inc, to control Power NZ. The agreement ends the pair's 2-1/2 year battle for control.
"What this represents is an acceptance by both of us that neither was going to get a breakthrough," Gilbert said of the decision to form a joint venture with Utilicorp NZ.
"Reaching an accommodation with each other was a better proposition than continuing to stage a battle in which neither of us could prevail."
The joint venture would need permission from the anti-trust Commerce Commission for the proposal to proceed.
"The arrangements are subject to approval by the Commerce Commission and the Overseas Investment Commission," he said.

Gilbert denied Mercury had paid too much for the Power NZ shares it already owns, saying the average purchase price was well under NZ$5 per share against $6 being offered minorities as part of today's announcement.
Mercury holds 33 percent of Power New Zealand and Utilicorp holds just over 33 percent.
Some 11 percent is held by the Waitemata Area Councils via the Power New Zealand Shareholders' Society.
Another 7.1 percent is held by the Thames-Coromandel, Matamata-Piako, South Waikato and Hauraki district councils.
Power NZ also has a 10 percent interest in WEL Energy Group Ltd, an electricity distributor in the neighbouring Waikato region.
Utilicorp had 39.5 percent of WEL and said it would sell that holding into the joint venture with Mercury.
Gilbert said there was no change in competition for electricity in Auckland as Power and Mercury would remain as separate entities.
Asked if Power and Mercury would eventually merge, Gilbert said: "No. That's the basis of the joint venture... that's inconsistent with a merger."

Gilbert said the previous logic of trying to buy Power NZ was to extract the financial benefits of a merger, which it estimated at NZ$30 million a year. PNZ had said benefits would only be $10 million.
"With a joint venture not all of those gains would be captured. Our view is that the gains will be somewhat less than $30 million, but nonetheless very substantial," Gilbert said.
The joint venture would be equity accounted within Mercury's books.
Gilbert said the rationalisation for the joint venture was that it was a sound investment.

"At the end of the day, if things go the way we would like, we would own 50 percent via the joint venture of a sound business. We would have bought that 50 percent at a reasonable price and the business would be highly efficient, well focused and well run."
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
